bull_case: High-cadence data becomes an infrastructure layer for governments and AI systems rather than a niche imagery purchase.
bear_case: Government procurement cycles, launch constraints and public/free imagery can cap pricing power.
thesis: Planet has structural leadership in high-cadence Earth observation: the long-lived data archive, daily scanning cadence and platform distribution create a distinct category position. Defense and sovereign demand is becoming an additional long-duration driver.

evidence.claim: Defense & Intelligence revenue was $180.232M in FY2026, the largest customer type.
August 2026 included NGA and German sovereign satellite-services awards.

counterevidence: Satellite services can raise revenue growth while also increasing hardware, launch and execution intensity versus pure imagery subscriptions.
unknowns: Normalized satellite-services gross margin, long-run owner FCF/share, and customer concentration after current sovereign contract ramp.
falsifiers: If NDR falls below 100%, RPO/backlog contract materially, or owner FCF/share turns persistently negative despite revenue growth, the thesis is downgraded.
next_checks: Next 10-Q: revenue mix, RPO/backlog, NDR, adjusted FCF, SBC, ATM issuance and capex

subscores.rationale: Defense intelligence, climate, supply-chain and infrastructure monitoring support multi-year demand.
Planet owns one of the largest daily global Earth-observation datasets and a high-revisit constellation.
Multiple end markets and sovereign programs diversify demand, though launch/regulatory exposure persists.

uncertainties.rationale: Rapid business-model mix shift and early profitability make long-run normalization uncertain.
